avoid_when: Avoid for content-heavy slides requiring bullets, charts, or detailed explanation.
Avoid when a strong visual, product image, or brand-led cover is needed.
Avoid for agenda, comparison, or process-oriented content.
families.description: A sparse formal cover slide featuring a prominent centered title banner, presenter and affiliation details, and a presentation date.
families.name: cover-hero
selection_hints: Use as an opening cover for a formal presentation, interview statement, or internal business briefing.
Choose when the cover needs a centered title, presenter details, organizational affiliation, and date.
Best suited to a restrained corporate presentation with minimal introductory information.

avoid_when: The presentation needs a detailed recap, next steps, or contact information.
The closing page must include visuals, multiple content blocks, or a call-to-action.
families.description: A minimalist closing page built around one large, centered two-line farewell statement.
families.name: closing-hero
selection_hints: Use as a simple final slide to conclude a formal presentation.
Choose when a prominent closing statement and invitation for feedback are sufficient.

avoid_when: Avoid for text-only narratives without a supporting visual.
Avoid when more than two parallel content sections or multiple data views are required.
Avoid for image galleries or full-bleed photography.
families.description: A titled content slide pairs a large supporting visual on the left with a detailed explanatory text block on the right.
families.name: content-split
selection_hints: Use for explaining a concept with one prominent diagram or image and an adjacent text description.
Choose when a clear title and balanced visual-text split are desired.
Suitable for technical, educational, biographical, or case-study content with one supporting visual.

avoid_when: Avoid for image-led storytelling or slides that need charts instead of a structured matrix.
Avoid when the content cannot be organized into a moderately large table.
Avoid for minimal, single-message presentations without detailed supporting information.
families.description: A structured content slide pairs a prominent heading with a large comparison table and a rounded takeaway callout.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for a detailed matrix, scorecard, specification table, or multi-category comparison.
Use when a structured table needs a clearly emphasized takeaway beneath it.
Best for evidence-heavy content with one headline and one concluding insight.

avoid_when: Avoid when the content requires visuals, data charts, tables, or multiple parallel sections.
Avoid when there are too many detailed points to fit legibly in one large text block.
families.description: A conventional content slide with a strong top title band and one spacious bulleted text area below.
families.name: content-title_body
selection_hints: Use for a straightforward informational slide with a clear heading and a single bulleted list.
Suitable for presenting several related points where one item may need a longer explanation.

avoid_when: The presentation needs a visual agenda with images, section descriptions, or complex navigation.
There are more agenda items than can remain legible in a single vertical list.
families.description: A clean agenda slide with a prominent blue title banner and a spacious numbered list of presentation sections.
families.name: agenda-title_body
selection_hints: Use for an early presentation agenda with a clear title and a short ordered list of sections.
Choose when a simple, formal table of contents is preferred over a graphical roadmap.
